   validated against its closed model, and its `project_id` and `source_id` must equal those of its

topics.topic: Record durability boundary and post-rename synchronization failure semantics
questions: Which file and directory synchronizations constitute “made durable,” including newly created parent folders, and at what point may the operation report success for a record?

If the final rename succeeds but the subsequent durability synchronization fails, is the write reported as failed while the new file remains, is the old address restored, or is the operation treated as having taken effect?
Does “in place” mean that the rename succeeded, or that the record and its containing directory have also been synchronized so an acknowledged operation survives a host crash?

quotes:
Each stored image and record is written atomically: a reader sees the complete file or none, and a
   write that fails leaves the earlier state of its address as it was. A stored image is made durable
   before the record that refers to it is written, so a crash never leaves a record without its image; a
   failure to make it durable fails that write and A3 rule 5 condition 5 applies. A record is the last
   write of its operation: once it is in place the operation has taken effect.
judgement.why: The rule fixes the observable durability boundary and failure result: failed durability is a failed write preserving the earlier address, the image must be durable before its record, and the record being in place is the operation's effect point; the particular synchronization calls are implementation detail.

precedent.topic: Behavior when a valid mark record has no corresponding placement record
quotes:
`capability:delivery_store.read_placement` and `capability:delivery_store.read_mark` read both records, so a
   damaged record stops the delivery. With an existing placement the flow answers `replayed`, with the `photo_id` of
   its mark if there is one.
`capability:source_folder.read_named_source` applies condition 1 of A3 rule 5 and reads the file once.
`capability:delivery_store.write_placement` writes the record, and the lock is released.
precedent.why: The later delivery flow reads both records, stops only for a damaged record, replays only when a placement exists, and otherwise continues through source reading and placement writing; a schema-valid orphan mark is therefore retained while the missing placement is created.

quotes:
`capability:delivery_store.read_placement` and `capability:delivery_store.read_mark` read both records, so a
   damaged record stops the delivery. With an existing placement the flow answers `replayed`, with the `photo_id` of
   its mark if there is one.
`capability:source_folder.read_named_source` applies condition 1 of A3 rule 5 and reads the file once.
judgement.why: The delivery flow reads and validates both records before it reads the named source, so a damaged orphan mark produces state_unavailable before a missing or invalid name can produce NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT.

topics.topic: Missing-folder creation order, races, collisions, modes, and failures
questions: In what order and with what collision, race, mode-setting and failure rules are missing folders created?

Which folders are created, in what order, how are concurrent creations handled, what happens for an existing non-folder or symbolic link at any segment, and which answer is returned for each creation or mode-setting failure?

quotes:
The installation creates the binary
   store and the state folder; the service creates only folders below them, with the imported
   `STORE_FOLDER_MODE` and `STATE_FOLDER_MODE` constants, and removes none. Below the state folder the
   service follows no symbolic link.
judgement.divergence: When concurrent calls need the same missing folder, one implementation accepts the directory created by its competitor and continues while another treats the lost creation race as failure; the caller sees success versus refusal or file failure.
judgement.why: The rule states ownership, modes and no-link behavior but leaves folder order, race handling, collision classification and failure precedence open.

witness.initial: The installation-created state folder exists, but a project subfolder needed by two concurrent deliveries does not.
events: Two callers concurrently deliver content for the same project.
Both processes attempt to establish the missing service-owned folder.
outcomes: The process that loses the creation race verifies the newly existing directory and continues.
The process that loses the race treats the existing entry as a creation failure and returns a failure.
witness.observer: One caller sees successful processing versus failure.
basis:
Deliveries and marks of one project run one at a time, across processes, under an operating
   system lock on one lock file of that project in the state folder.

The installation creates the binary
   store and the state folder; the service creates only folders below them, with the imported

topics.topic: Mode requirements for pre-existing folders
questions: Do those constants govern only folders newly created by the service, or must an existing folder be checked or changed to that mode?
Are the constants enforced only on newly created folders, or must existing folders be checked or changed to those modes?

quotes:
The installation creates the binary
   store and the state folder; the service creates only folders below them, with the imported
   `STORE_FOLDER_MODE` and `STATE_FOLDER_MODE` constants, and removes none.
judgement.why: The sentence attaches the mode constants to folders the service creates; it does not impose a check or chmod operation on pre-existing folders.

topics.topic: Project-lock primitive, scope, and release time
questions: Does the holder end when the individual delivery or mark operation finishes, when its request task is cancelled, or only when the process exits?
Which operating-system locking primitive and lock scope must all processes use, and when exactly is the lock released?

quotes: A held lock for the duration of the caller's block.
The lock is released on every path.
judgement.why: The later operation contract fixes operation/block scope and the flow fixes release on every exit; the particular operating-system primitive remains immaterial under P8 so long as it enforces cross-process serialization.

topics.topic: Whether no-write replay or failed-delivery paths may create locks or folders
questions: Does “the project lock” include any newly created parent folders, or must the chosen lock address require no additional folder write during a failed delivery?
If a valid placement exists but its project lock does not, must replay create the lock or write nothing?
What must the Required tests item assert to demonstrate the invariant's full claim that a repeated placement writes nothing, including lock files, state folders, mark records and temporary files?

quotes:
Conditions 1 to 4 write nothing except the
   project lock (A6 rule 4).

The lock file is created on first
   use with the imported `LOCK_FILE_MODE` constant and is never changed or removed afterwards.

The installation creates the binary
   store and the state folder; the service creates only folders below them, with the imported
   `STORE_FOLDER_MODE` and `STATE_FOLDER_MODE` constants, and removes none.

INV-06: a second placement returns the first publication and leaves every stored image and placement record unchanged, with one placement record in place (`test_a_repeated_placement_writes_no_durable_state`).
judgement.divergence: On a first failed delivery with no lock-directory hierarchy, one implementation creates the lock parent and lock file before returning the file failure while another treats the missing parent as state_unavailable or uses a direct lock address; the caller and owner see different results and durable changes.
judgement.why: The texts do not say whether project-lock writes include creation of parent folders, while the Required tests item also enumerates only stored images and placement records rather than everything covered by the no-write claim.

witness.initial: The installation-created state folder is empty, the project connection is confirmed, and the requested source name is absent.
events: The caller requests delivery for the project and source id.
The service reaches the project-lock step before checking the named source.
outcomes: The service creates a lock parent folder and lock file, then returns NOT_READY_OR_ABSENT.
The service refuses because the lock parent is absent or uses a layout requiring no parent-folder creation.
witness.observer: The caller may see a different response and the owner sees a different state-folder change.
basis:
Checks run in this order: token, request form and project id, connection, photo folder, source id,
   project lock, existing placement, named file.

topics.topic: Accepted EXIF date-time byte and text grammar
questions: What exact byte or text grammar is accepted for EXIF `DateTimeOriginal` and `DateTime`, including whitespace, fractional seconds, NUL padding, and out-of-range calendar fields?

quotes:
A camera value is unusable when it is malformed, when its UTC year
   is before 2000, or when it is more than 24 hours after the file's modification time.
judgement.divergence: A strict parser can reject a padded or fractional EXIF timestamp and fall back to the file modification time, while a permissive parser can accept it as the camera instant; the calling flow and Portal observe different photo_date and date_source values.
judgement.why: The word malformed does not define the accepted EXIF byte/text grammar, whitespace, padding, fractional-second or calendar-field rules.

witness.initial: A deliverable image contains a padded EXIF DateTimeOriginal value and has a different modification time.
events: The deliverer selects the first usable photo moment.
outcomes: A strict parser rejects the padded camera value and uses the modification time.
A permissive parser trims the padding and uses the EXIF camera time.
witness.observer: The calling flow and Portal see different photo_date and date_source values.
basis: The source may be JPEG, PNG or WEBP.

The photo moment is the first usable value of: EXIF `DateTimeOriginal`, EXIF `DateTime`, then
   the file's modification time.

topics.topic: Atomic replacement visibility for an existing destination file
questions: When a complete file already exists at the destination, must readers continuously see either the old or new complete file, or may they transiently see no file?

quotes:
Each stored image and record is written atomically: a reader sees the complete file or none, and a
   write that fails leaves the earlier state of its address as it was.
judgement.divergence: During successful replacement of an existing orphan image, one implementation preserves continuous old-or-new visibility while another briefly removes the destination and exposes no file; the Portal notices a successful read versus a missing binary.
judgement.why: The complete-file-or-none rule does not state whether a successful replacement of an already existing destination may include a transient absent interval.

witness.initial: A failed record write has left a complete stored image at the final address without a placement record.
events: The caller repeats delivery of the same source.
The deliverer writes the stored image again while the Portal reads its final reference.
outcomes: The Portal continuously sees either the complete old image or the complete new image.
The Portal observes no file during a remove-then-rename replacement.
witness.observer: The Portal and its client request see a complete image versus a missing binary.
basis:
After condition 5 a stored image may remain without a record: no caller has received
   its reference, and a repeated delivery of the same file writes it again and completes the placement,
   unless a refusal of A6 rule 5 applies.

The Portal reads a stored image and alone decides who may retrieve
   it.

topics.topic: Behavior when the system clock fails or violates its contract
questions: What must a mark do if `utc_now` fails or returns a value outside the required naive-UTC datetime contract?

quotes:
### Errors

None.
The current time in UTC without an offset, in microseconds.
judgement.why: The later utc_now operation contract permits no error and guarantees the required output form, so a raised error or out-of-contract value is not an admissible operation outcome for generated callers to classify.

topics.topic: Classification of missing record ancestors versus inaccessible state
questions: If the state folder or an ancestor of a record address is missing at runtime, is the record absent, is the operation refused as state unavailable, or does the service recreate anything?
How is absence distinguished from an inability to inspect the address or one of its parent folders?

quotes:
The installation creates the binary
   store and the state folder; the service creates only folders below them, with the imported
   `STORE_FOLDER_MODE` and `STATE_FOLDER_MODE` constants, and removes none.
A record is absent only when nothing exists at its address.

A record that is a symbolic link, that cannot be read, or that fails that validation is never
   taken for an absent record: the operation is refused with the STATE_UNAVAILABLE member of
   = models.RefusalCode, whose value is `state_unavailable`, and changes no record and no stored image.
judgement.why: The texts make the installation create the state root and say the service never removes it, but provide no admissible history in which that root disappears; inaccessible existing record state is already answered as state_unavailable.

topics.topic: Filesystem actions required to make an image durable
questions: What filesystem actions constitute making the image durable, including newly created parent folders and the rename into its final address?

quotes:
A stored image is made durable
   before the record that refers to it is written, so a crash never leaves a record without its image; a
   failure to make it durable fails that write and A3 rule 5 condition 5 applies.
judgement.why: Any filesystem sequence is acceptable if it satisfies the specified crash-survival and failure guarantees; a sequence that can leave a surviving record without its image violates the quoted rule rather than representing an allowed alternative.

topics.topic: Required record file type and symbolic-link handling
questions: Must an existing record be a regular file opened without following links, and how are directories, devices, sockets and FIFOs handled?

quotes:
A record is absent only when nothing exists at its address. A placement or mark record that exists is
   validated against its closed model, and its `project_id` and `source_id` must equal those of its
   address. A record that is a symbolic link, that cannot be read, or that fails that validation is never
   taken for an absent record: the operation is refused with the STATE_UNAVAILABLE member of
   = models.RefusalCode, whose value is `state_unavailable`, and changes no record and no stored image.
judgement.divergence: For a FIFO or other non-regular object at a record address, one implementation rejects its type immediately with state_unavailable while another opens it as readable input and can block or parse supplied bytes; the caller observes immediate refusal versus delay or normal processing.
judgement.why: The rule explicitly handles symbolic links and unreadable or invalid records but does not require a regular file or a non-blocking, no-follow open for every other filesystem object type.

The service opens the FIFO for reading and waits for a writer or validates bytes supplied through it.
witness.observer: The caller observes an immediate refusal versus a blocked or normally processed request.
